# Agent Skills Checked Into the Repo

The tooling that *builds* the product is committed **alongside** the product, versioned with it and
reviewed like it. In [[stickfps]] that is 91 files under `.tooling/` — more files than the server
source directory.

Two different things live there, and the distinction matters:

**Vendored (87 files).** Nineteen Three.js skill packs, each a `SKILL.md` plus
`references/{methods,examples,anti-patterns}.md`. Third-party, with provenance in frontmatter —
`license: MIT`, `metadata.author: OpenAEC-Foundation`. Taxonomy is five prefixes: `core-` (math,
raycaster, renderer, scene-graph), `syntax-` (geometries, materials, shaders, controls), `impl-`
(react-three-fiber, drei, lighting, shadows, animation, audio, post-processing), `errors-`
(performance, rendering), `agents-` (scene-builder, model-optimizer). The content is reference tables
and NEVER/ALWAYS rules aimed squarely at model failure modes rather than at human learning:

> "Designed for AI coding agents."
> — browser_game_stickfps/.tooling/skills/ (SKILL.md frontmatter), 2026-07-25

**Authored (4 files).** Three subagent definitions and one orchestration command — see
[[architect-coder-tester-loop]], which is where the role separation is documented.

## Why commit it

Committing the tooling makes the build process *reproducible* in the same sense the code is: a later
session, or another person, starts from the same instructions rather than from whatever the model
happens to know. It also makes the instructions **reviewable** — a wrong rule in a skill pack is a
diff, not an invisible habit.

The seed directory `files/` extends the same idea backwards: pristine copies of `TASKS.md`, an empty
`PROGRESS.md` skeleton and the four agent files, all stamped 2026-07-14, kept in the repo as a
bootstrap kit. `TODO:` whether `files/` is a deliberate reusable kit for future projects or leftover
scaffolding was not resolved at interview — no intent is asserted here.

## The cost: vendored knowledge drifts too

Skill packs are pinned text about a moving dependency, and nothing checks them against the lockfile.
The R3F pack states a version floor the project has already passed:

> "Requires @react-three/fiber 8.x+"
> — browser_game_stickfps/.tooling/skills/impl-react-three-fiber/SKILL.md, 2026-07-25

More seriously, all four **authored** files still instruct agents to use Geckos.io and Fly.io, months
after both were replaced in [[websocket-tcp-over-geckos-udp]] and [[render-over-fly-io]]. Guidance
that is confidently wrong is worse than absent guidance, because the loop reads it as authoritative.
Catalogued with the rest in [[documentation-drift]].

## Confidence

`confidence: medium` — the artefacts are directly observed and unambiguous, but this appears in
**one repository only** so far, which is thin evidence for a *pattern* in the user's practice rather
than a one-off. `TODO:` whether the skill packs actually changed what got written, and where the 19
packs came from, is unanswered.
